working_definition: T2a is a columnar T-type neuron of the adult Drosophila optic lobe whose soma lies posteriorly adjacent to the gap between the medulla and lobula plate. The cell body fiber projects along the proximal medulla surface, bifurcates in the second optic chiasm, and sends one branch into a medulla column (bushy arborization in M9, fine arbors throughout M1-M4 with bifurcation at M5) and another branch to lobula layer 3 where it forms a bleb-type terminal arborization wider than a single column. Identity assigned in the atlas by transcriptional similarity to T2 and T3; the anatomical name T2a originates with Fischbach and Dittrich (1989).

best_match.fbbt_definition: T neuron with its soma posteriorly adjacent to the gap between the medulla and lobula plate and a cell body fiber that projects along the proximal surface of the medulla before branching in the second optic chiasm (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989; Shinomiya et al., 2019). One branch projects into a medulla column, where it forms a bushy, fine, arborization in medulla layer M9 and then projects through the rest of the medulla column, bifurcating in medulla layer M5 and forming fine arbors throughout layers M1-4. The other branch forms a terminal arborization in lobula layer 3 that is much wider than a single column and has bleb-type terminal branches.

justification: FBbt:00003729 'T2a neuron' is defined as a T neuron with soma adjacent to the medulla/lobula-plate gap, cell body fiber along the proximal medulla surface, bifurcation in the second optic chiasm, medulla arborisations in M9 (bushy) and M1-M4 (fine, bifurcating at M5), and a wide bleb-type terminal in lobula layer 3 (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989; Shinomiya et al., 2019). The atlas cluster 'T2a' carries the identical canonical anatomical name and was assigned by the authors on the basis of transcriptional similarity to T2/T3, referring to the same Fischbach and Dittrich morphological series. The label is a direct anatomical name (not a driver alias), the FBbt term is not obsolete, and no feature distinguishing the cluster falls outside the FBbt definition. The match is therefore exact.

other_candidates.fbbt_definition: Intrinsic columnar neuron of the optic lobe that has its cell body in the posterior part of the optic lobe and a cell body fiber that bifurcates in the second optic chiasma (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989). It has two branches, each targeting a different neuropil adjacent to the second optic chiasma (lobula, lobula plate and medulla) (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989).
